{"body":"﻿## Mission
Animate the four operator-selected characters as real Tiny3D outputs with visible motion, not just contracts/metadata. Reuse the exact valid LowVRAM/Tiny3D source geometry when it exists; downstream rig/animation work must not trigger geometry regeneration unless the upstream asset is independently proven invalid or missing.

This is a concrete asset-delivery slice under the existing animation/secondary-motion/rendered-proof owners (#133, #19, #20, #13). Do not create another planner, proof framework, queue, or parallel animation pipeline.

## Operator-selected source identities
These 12-view sheets are the required visual identities to match before rigging. Match each to its exact producer/library asset by provenance/hash; do not guess from display names.

1. `weqww_03_highly_detailed_ultra_realistic_character_2b1_variant_b__views12_FULL.png`
   - sheet SHA-256 `be589af00f8e1bd74b7ab9e73d46e00362b7465c2b3e2a6cc3826780df7fcca4`
   - bird/pelican-like robed character with carried bags/cloth
2. `weqww_05_seremonialinen_yoperhosolento_sauvoineen_variant_b__views12_FULL.png`
   - sheet SHA-256 `a377cc2d49407303ba11ff73a57e7146e769d4dce821b232459a98ed9fbc476e`
   - ceremonial moth/insect character with staff and large wings
3. `weqww_07_clean_high_res_fantasy_character_9b9_variant_b__views12_FULL.png`
   - sheet SHA-256 `7f8a16eba8a14c5541307909fcc009d30dbecd04be94c0aed8752bdd96358d62`
   - tall ethereal humanoid with long ribbon/tendril forms
4. `sadetakkihahmo__views12_FULL.png`
   - sheet SHA-256 `0372e9c28ebf89a615848e18f7ecd27f3bd118b58ff8f787178796de71bd8207`
   - hooded raincoat character with scarf/coat hems

## Required visible motion
All four must have a visibly nontrivial idle/presentation animation and an actual head/look turn where the anatomy supports it.

1. Bird character: head/neck look turn, subtle body/weight idle, visible secondary motion on loose robe/bags/feather-like regions where topology permits.
2. Moth character: **hero airborne proof**. Wings must spread from a resting pose, perform repeated flapping, and the character must hover visibly off the ground with subtle vertical/root motion. Staff/body motion must remain coherent rather than sliding independently.
3. Ethereal humanoid: head/upper-body look turn plus controlled flowing secondary motion through the long ribbon/tendril/skirt forms; avoid rigid whole-mesh wobble.
4. Raincoat character: hood/head look turn, subtle body idle, and readable scarf/coat-hem secondary motion while the boots remain planted for the grounded clip.

## Implementation approach
Inspect the real mesh topology/material/components first, then use the lightest correct existing Tiny3D mechanism per moving region:

- articulated head/neck/wings/limbs -> bones + skin weights;
- loose cloth, feathers, ribbons, tendrils -> existing secondary-motion owner, adding distributed bones/curve/lattice/shape-key deformation only where current skinning cannot produce clean motion;
- hover -> root/body transform layered with local wing/body animation;
- rigid accessories -> parented rigid motion or dedicated bones, not smeared skin weights.

Extend the current body-plan/animation-adapter/secondary-motion/animation-quality/repair owners when a reusable gap is found. A new method counts as a pipeline improvement only if it is exercised successfully on at least two of these assets or fixes a clearly recurring class of failure. Otherwise keep the change asset-local.

## Proof chain
For each asset preserve one traceable chain:

`SOURCE -> SEGMENTATION -> HIGHLIGHTED MOVING REGIONS -> RIG/BONES/WEIGHTS -> REPRESENTATIVE ANIMATION FRAMES -> FULL MOTION -> VISUAL VERDICT`

Required evidence per asset:

- exact upstream mesh/provenance hash and Tiny3D asset/compiler identity;
- segmentation/moving-region visualization before final rig acceptance;
- inspectable skeleton/weights or equivalent deformation setup;
- representative frames showing neutral + extrema (head turn; wing spread/flap for moth; secondary-motion extrema);
- deterministic animation-quality receipt using the existing quality gate where applicable;
- full rendered motion proof through the existing canonical rendered-proof path;
- direct visual review result tied to the exact artifact/commit/state.

## Visual acceptance
PASS requires the rendered motion itself to look correct. Structural/numeric PASS alone is insufficient.

Reject proof with any of the following: wrong source identity, stale artifact, wrong camera, hidden wings/head, severe mesh collapse, obvious weight smearing, major new self-intersection, foot sliding/floating on grounded clips, accessories detaching, rigid cloth/tendrils when secondary motion is required, hover character touching the ground throughout, or a video that does not visibly show the claimed motion.

The moth hero clip must clearly show: wings initially less spread -> visible spread -> repeated flap cycles while airborne -> stable coherent hover/readable silhouette.

## User-deliverable proof
Deliver user-openable visual proof, not paths or claims:

- one concise MP4 per asset (or one clearly chaptered MP4 containing all four);
- one contact sheet / representative-frame sheet per asset;
- verify delivered bytes end-to-end with file size + SHA-256 using the already proven transfer route.

Do not regenerate captures repeatedly because transport failed; repair/use the proven transfer path.

## Done when
- [ ] Exact 3D source identity for all 4 operator-selected characters is proven.
- [ ] All 4 have visibly useful animation, including head/look motion.
- [ ] Moth has proven wing spread + repeated flap + real airborne hover.
- [ ] Loose regions receive visibly appropriate secondary motion where applicable.
- [ ] Existing deterministic quality checks pass for the claims they cover.
- [ ] Direct visual review passes the exact rendered clips.
- [ ] User can actually open the delivered proof bytes; size + SHA-256 are verified.
- [ ] Any reusable pipeline improvement is integrated into the existing owner and proven on >=2 selected assets; no duplicate mechanism remains.
- [ ] P3 runtime/gameplay remains explicitly separate unless real P3 proof is returned; do not imply it from Tiny3D renders.

## Anti-churn constraints
Work asset-by-asset and preserve valid intermediate results. Do not rerun LowVRAM generation for Tiny3D rig/render failures. Do not create one-off proof scripts when the canonical proof owner can be extended. Do not repeat unchanged animation-repair attempts. Do not spend the mission on reports, policy, queues, or broad architecture cleanup unless a concrete defect blocks these four visible deliveries.
